outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the Brumer–Stark part has been claimed complete: a preprint (arXiv:2310.16399, posted 25 Oct 2023, before the window) gives a 'complete proof of the Brumer-Stark conjecture over Z', with no journal acceptance, referee report or public check found; the earlier Annals-published proof covers every prime except 2. Within the window, only partial Stark-type work and revisions appeared (Zhang v4 Jun 2024; Nickel PAMS 2024; Padrés thesis 2024; Honnor v3 Dec 2025; Dasgupta–Honnor–Spieß JLMS Oct 2025; Bullach–Macías Castillo 2025; Black dissertation 2025), and the general Stark conjecture for Artin L-functions at s=0 shows no proof found.
problem_asks: Two parts, unpacked from the January 2024 statement 'Stark conjectures (including Brumer–Stark conjecture)'. (1) The Stark conjectures in general: for a Galois extension K/k of number fields and its Artin L-function, (a) the leading Taylor coefficient at s=0 is predicted to equal, up to an algebraic or rational factor, a Stark regulator built from units or S-units; (b) the rank-one abelian refinement predicts Stark units whose values generate abelian extensions of k; (c) the higher-order-vanishing refinements (Rubin, Popescu-type); (d) the non-abelian case. (2) The Brumer–Stark conjecture, named explicitly: for a finite abelian extension H/F, certain Stickelberger-type elements annihilate the (T-smoothed) class group, equivalently Brumer–Stark units with prescribed valuations exist; the Wikipedia lead describes it as a special case of Stark's conjecture where the completely split place is finite. Scope of (2) for non-CM abelian extensions was not checked against the Wikipedia wording.

events.what_happened: Harold Stark's rank-one abelian conjecture is recorded (per Wikipedia's Stark conjectures article, citing Stark, Advances in Mathematics 35, 1980) as proved for base fields Q and imaginary quadratic fields only. I did not open the 1980 paper; the claim rests on that Wikipedia sentence.
events.delivers: Rank-one abelian case of the Stark conjecture (leading coefficient and Stark units) when the base field is Q or an imaginary quadratic field, per Wikipedia. The statement is not verified against the 1980 paper.
events.remains: The rank-one abelian case over all other base number fields; higher-order vanishing; non-abelian extensions; the Brumer–Stark statement beyond the cases covered.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (per Wikipedia reference; not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the Stark prediction in the listed cases (leading term matches a Stark regulator and Stark units exist).

events.what_happened: The function-field analogue of the Brumer–Stark conjecture is recorded (per Wikipedia's Brumer–Stark article) as proved by John Tate and Pierre Deligne in 1984 (Tate, Les conjectures de Stark sur les fonctions L d'Artin en s=0, Progress in Mathematics 47, 1984), with a second proof by David Hayes (Compositio Mathematica 55, 1985). Not opened; Wikipedia is the only source.
events.delivers: Function-field analogue of Brumer–Stark and of Stark's conjecture at s=0 for abelian extensions of function fields over finite fields (per Wikipedia). This is an analogue in a different setting.
events.remains: The number-field Brumer–Stark conjecture and the number-field Stark conjectures.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published proofs (per Wikipedia citations; not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture, but only for the function-field analogue.

events.what_happened: Mazur and Rubin, 'Refined class number formulas for G_m' (arXiv:1312.4053, v1 14 Dec 2013; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Stark-type refined class number formula; they prove a large part of the conjecture using Kolyvagin systems, but only when the order of vanishing is 1.
events.delivers: A large part of a refined Stark-type class number conjecture, conditional on the order of vanishing of the associated L-function being 1.
events.remains: The order-of-vanishing statement beyond order 1, and the full leading-term statement without the order-1 assumption.
events.direction: Partial confirmation of a Stark-type refinement, under an extra hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Popescu, 'On a refined Stark conjecture for function fields' (arXiv:math/9701208, v1 6 Jan 1997, MSRI 1997-002; published Compositio Mathematica 116, 1999 per Wikipedia). Proves a refinement of Stark's conjecture formulated by Rubin, for finite abelian extensions of function fields over finite fields.
events.delivers: Rubin's refinement of Stark's conjecture, true up to primes dividing the order of the Galois group, for finite abelian extensions of function fields over finite fields; a stronger statement for constant-field extensions. Function-field analogue only.
events.remains: The number-field version of Rubin's refinement; the prime divisors of the group order are excluded.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (per Wikipedia reference; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Confirms Rubin's refinement, up to primes dividing the group order, in the function-field setting.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, Kakde and Ventullo, 'On the Gross-Stark Conjecture' (arXiv:1605.08169, v1 26 May 2016; single version). Proves Gross's 1980 conjecture on the leading term at s=0 of the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function (the p-adic Gross–Stark statement). Published in Annals 188 (2018) per Wikipedia; journal not opened.
events.delivers: Gross's p-adic conjecture for the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function (the Gross–Stark statement). A p-adic analogue of the Stark leading-term problem, not the complex Stark conjecture.
events.remains: The complex Stark and Brumer–Stark statements.
events.direction: Confirms Gross's p-adic conjecture, an analogue of the Stark problem.

events.what_happened: Darmon, Dasgupta and Pollack proved the Gross–Stark conjecture conditionally in 2011 (Annals 174), per Wikipedia's Stark conjectures article. Not opened; recorded because it is a p-adic Stark-type result that predates the window.
events.delivers: Gross–Stark conjecture for the relevant case, conditionally (per Wikipedia). p-adic analogue.
events.remains: Unconditional case (superseded by the 2016 Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo entry); complex Stark and Brumer–Stark.
events.direction: Confirms a conditional p-adic analogue.

events.what_happened: Johnston and Nickel, 'On the non-abelian Brumer-Stark conjecture and the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture' (arXiv:1509.00200). Known only from a search-result summary; not opened. Reports that, for odd p, p-primary parts of refinements of the non-abelian Brumer and Brumer–Stark conjectures follow from the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture for totally real fields, giving unconditional proofs in many new cases.
events.delivers: Per summary: p-primary parts of non-abelian Brumer and Brumer–Stark refinements, for odd p, conditional on the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture, unconditional in many cases. Non-abelian generalisation of Brumer–Stark.
events.remains: The abelian Brumer–Stark conjecture as stated; the p=2 part; the non-abelian conjecture in general.
events.direction: Partial confirmation of non-abelian refinements, under the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture.

events.what_happened: Johnston and Nickel, 'On the p-adic Stark conjecture at s=1 and applications' (arXiv:1703.06803; v1 20 Mar 2017, v5 14 Oct 2019). Accepted to appear in Journal of the London Mathematical Society (DOI 10.1112/jlms.12310) per v5 comment.
events.revisions: v2 21 Apr 2017; v3 13 Sep 2018; v4 11 Feb 2019; v5 14 Oct 2019 (accepted version per comment).
events.delivers: p-adic Stark conjecture at s=1 unconditionally when E/Q is abelian; conditional on Leopoldt's conjecture for some non-abelian extensions. The paper also notes that for fixed p the p-adic statement implies Stark's conjecture at s=1. This is a p-adic analogue at s=1, not the complex Stark conjecture at s=0.
events.remains: The complex Stark conjecture at s=0; non-abelian cases without Leopoldt.

checked_by.who: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (stated in arXiv v5 comment; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Confirms a p-adic analogue at s=1 in the abelian-over-Q case; a different statement from the complex Stark conjecture.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta and Spieß, 'The Eisenstein cocycle, partial zeta values and Gross–Stark units' (arXiv:1411.4025, Nov 2014; published as 'Partial zeta values, Gross's tower of fields conjecture, and Gross–Stark units', J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20 (2018), 2643–2683). Proves a Gross conjecture on the order of vanishing of Stickelberger elements in an abelian tower of fields and gives a cohomological construction of Gross–Stark units. Known from search results; the arXiv page was not opened.
events.delivers: Gross's order-of-vanishing conjecture for Stickelberger elements in an abelian tower of fields (per search summary). Adjacent to Brumer–Stark: a tower-of-fields analogue.
events.remains: The tower-of-fields conjecture beyond the proved order-of-vanishing statement; Brumer–Stark over Z; Stark in general.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (journal listing via search result; not opened)

events.direction: Confirms a Gross-type tower-of-fields order-of-vanishing statement; adjacent rather than the Brumer–Stark statement.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta and Kakde, 'On the Brumer-Stark Conjecture' (arXiv:2010.00657; v1 1 Oct 2020, v2 6 Nov 2020, v3 5 Sep 2022). Published as 'On the Brumer–Stark conjecture', Annals of Mathematics 197(1) (2023), 289–388, online 22 Nov 2022 (DOI 10.4007/annals.2023.197.1.5). Opened the arXiv abstract and the Annals page.
events.revisions: v2 6 Nov 2020; v3 5 Sep 2022 (reference updated); Annals 197(1), 2023 (online 22 Nov 2022).
events.delivers: Brumer–Stark conjecture for finite abelian H/F, F totally real and H CM, after tensoring with Z[1/2], i.e. every prime except 2. Also Kurihara's stronger Fitting-ideal formula in terms of Stickelberger elements, and Rubin's higher-rank version, both away from 2. Restricted to the Z[1/2] setting.
events.remains: The p=2 component of Brumer–Stark (i.e. the statement over Z); the stronger Kurihara-type statement at 2; Stark conjectures in general.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (editorial and referee process)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record in the field
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Annals 197(1), 289–388 (2023)

events.direction: Confirms the Brumer–Stark conjecture away from 2 (and the Kurihara and Rubin variants away from 2), so it cuts in the direction the conjecture asserts.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta and Kakde, 'Brumer-Stark Units and Explicit Class Field Theory' (arXiv:2103.02516; v1 3 Mar 2021; v2 25 Jul 2023, 'to appear in Duke Math. J.'). Proves the p-part (odd p) of the integral Gross–Stark conjecture for Brumer–Stark p-units in CM abelian extensions of totally real F, and deduces that the Brumer–Stark units plus n−1 square roots generate the maximal abelian extension of F. Published in Duke Math. J. 173(8) (2024) per search-result summaries (journal page not opened). The journal date does not move the event date.
events.revisions: v2 25 Jul 2023; Duke Math. J. 173(8) (2024) per search summary.
events.delivers: p-part, for odd primes p, of the integral Gross–Stark conjecture for Brumer–Stark p-units in CM abelian extensions of a totally real field, plus the Hilbert-12th-type generation statement (described by the authors as unconditional but involving p-adic integration over infinitely many primes). A Gross–Stark refinement, not the Brumer–Stark conjecture itself.
events.remains: The p=2 case of the integral Gross–Stark statement; the Brumer–Stark conjecture as stated (the unit construction is a consequence, not the annihilation statement).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as 'to appear' (v2) and in volume 173(8) (2024) per search summary

events.direction: Confirms an integral Gross–Stark refinement for odd p and the unit-generation consequence; does not decide the Brumer–Stark conjecture at 2.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta and Kakde, 'On the Brumer-Stark Conjecture and Refinements' (arXiv:2204.09037, v1 19 Apr 2022), an ICM 2022 survey (DOI 10.4171/icm2022/124). Restates that the Brumer–Stark, Rubin higher-rank and Kurihara statements are proved away from 2, and reports partial results toward Gross's conjecture and an exact p-adic formula for Brumer–Stark units.
events.delivers: Restatement of the away-from-2 results; no new mathematics claimed in the abstract summary.
events.remains: Prime 2; Stark in general.
events.direction: Consistent with the away-from-2 result; no new cut.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, Honnor and Spieß, 'On the Equality of Three Formulas for Brumer–Stark Units' (arXiv:2211.01715). v1 posted 3 Nov 2022 with authors Dasgupta and Honnor (per the v1 page); the current version lists Dasgupta, Honnor and Spieß (v2 15 Dec 2025, v3 17 Dec 2025). Published in J. London Math. Soc. 112(4), Oct 2025 (DOI 10.1112/jlms.70296 per search summary).
events.revisions: v2 15 Dec 2025; v3 17 Dec 2025 (after the window); JLMS 112(4), Oct 2025.
events.delivers: Proves the equality of three conjectural formulas for the Brumer–Stark units. Because the first formula is 'essentially proven' (Dasgupta–Kakde), it also verifies the validity of the other two. Concerns explicit unit formulas (refinement), not the Stickelberger annihilation statement.
events.remains: Whether the first formula is fully proven, including at the prime 2 (the 'essentially' qualifier); the Brumer–Stark conjecture as an annihilation statement.

checked_by.who: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, vol. 112 no. 4 (Oct 2025) per search summary; journal page not opened

events.doubts: The qualifier 'essentially proven' is the authors' own wording and leaves open whether the first formula is complete at the prime 2. Not an objection, but it bounds the claim.
events.direction: Confirms equality of three unit formulas; if the first formula is complete, the other two follow.

events.what_happened: Honnor, 'On the Root of Unity Ambiguity in a Formula for the Brumer–Stark Units' (arXiv:2302.12332). v1 23 Feb 2023; v2 11 Jan 2024 (before the freeze); v3 17 Dec 2025 ('proves a stronger result, dealing with the ambiguity at 2'). The v1 abstract as displayed says the eTNC result of Bullach–Burns–Daoud–Seo implies the formulas are correct up to a 2-power root of unity, and the v3 abstract says the ambiguity is resolved. The v1 page may show a later abstract; the wording could not be confirmed as v1-specific.
events.revisions: v2 11 Jan 2024 (before the freeze); v3 17 Dec 2025 (inside the window): stronger result, ambiguity at 2 dealt with, one assumption removed.
events.delivers: A conjectural exact formula for the Brumer–Stark units is correct up to a root of unity (v1 as displayed); v3 is reported to resolve the ambiguity, including at 2 (abstract). Scope: unit formula, a refinement of Brumer–Stark, not the annihilation conjecture.
events.remains: The annihilation form of Brumer–Stark is not addressed by this paper; the v3 body was not read, so the exact remaining scope of the unit formula cannot be stated with confidence.
events.direction: Confirms the Brumer–Stark unit formula (up to root of unity in v1; stated as resolved in v3).

events.what_happened: Nickel, 'The strong Stark conjecture for totally odd characters' (arXiv:2106.05619; v1 10 Jun 2021). Proves the p-part of the strong Stark conjecture for every totally odd character and every odd prime p, and an unconditional minus p-part of the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for certain CM extensions with abelian Sylow p-subgroup and ramification restrictions. Published Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 152 (2024), 147–162.
events.revisions: Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 152 (2024) (journal, inside the window; date of first argument is 2021).
events.delivers: p-part of the strong Stark conjecture for totally odd characters, odd p. Restricted to totally odd characters; for the ETNC form, further ramification and Sylow-p restrictions.
events.remains: p=2; characters that are not totally odd; the general Stark conjecture.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, 152 (2024), 147–162 (per arXiv comment; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the strong Stark conjecture for totally odd characters at odd primes; cuts in the direction Stark asserts, in a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Robin Zhang, 'The Harris-Venkatesh conjecture for derived Hecke operators II: a unified Stark conjecture' (arXiv:2305.08956; v1 15 May 2023, v2 23 May 2023, v3 21 Nov 2023, v4 3 Jun 2024). Proves a compatibility theorem between the Stark conjecture and the Harris–Venkatesh conjecture for imaginary dihedral weight-one modular forms, and formulates a unified conjecture covering both.
events.revisions: v2 23 May 2023; v3 21 Nov 2023; v4 3 Jun 2024 (inside the window). No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: A compatibility theorem between the Stark and Harris–Venkatesh conjectures for imaginary dihedral weight-one forms; a unified conjecture. Does not, by the abstract, prove the Stark conjecture itself in those cases; it relates two conjectures.
events.remains: The Stark conjecture for general Galois representations; the unified conjecture; Brumer–Stark.
events.direction: Compatibility between two conjectures in a restricted class; does not decide Stark in those cases.

events.what_happened: Burns, Macías Castillo and Seo, 'On Weil-Stark elements, II: refined Stark conjectures' (arXiv:2310.10581; v1 16 Oct 2023; no journal reference). Develops an axiomatic approach to refined versions of Stark's conjecture using Weil–Stark elements; the abstract says it gives 'concrete new results concerning leading terms of Artin L-series and arithmetic properties of Stark elements'. The body was not read.
events.delivers: Per abstract: an axiomatic framework for refined Stark conjectures and unspecified new results on leading terms of Artin L-series. The specific cases are not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The Stark conjecture for general Artin L-functions; the specific cases produced are not identified here.
events.direction: Concerns refined forms of Stark's conjecture; the abstract does not state a cut.

events.what_happened: Bullach and Macías Castillo, 'Annihilating class groups in p-elementary extensions' (arXiv:2310.10468; v1 16 Oct 2023; no journal ref on arXiv). Derives new cases of conjectures of Rubin and of Burns–Kurihara–Sano on derivatives of Dirichlet L-series at s=0, in p-elementary abelian extensions for arbitrary p, giving annihilators of class groups from S-truncated Dirichlet L-series for large enough S. Published Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 179 (2025), 145–166, first online 19 May 2025 (per Cambridge record found by search; not opened). The PDF was not readable.
events.revisions: Journal version: Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 179 (2025), 145–166, first online 19 May 2025 (per search summary).
events.delivers: New cases, in p-elementary abelian extensions and with large enough S, of Rubin's higher-rank Stark-type conjecture and of the Burns–Kurihara–Sano conjecture (annihilation of class groups). Restricted class.
events.remains: The general Rubin and Burns–Kurihara–Sano conjectures; the cases outside p-elementary extensions.

checked_by.who: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, 179 (2025), 145–166 (per Cambridge record found by search; not opened)

events.doubts: One search summary of the 2025 journal version describes its main theorems as depending on an assumed conjecture for subextensions. I could not read the PDF to confirm this, so whether the 2023 cases are unconditional is unverified.
events.direction: Confirms new cases of Rubin's and BKS's Stark-type annihilation statements in a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, Kakde, Silliman and Wang, 'The Brumer–Stark Conjecture over Z' (arXiv:2310.16399; v1 submitted 25 Oct 2023; 56 pages). The abstract states: 'In this paper we give a complete proof of the Brumer-Stark conjecture over Z.' The arXiv abstract page lists only v1; the v2 URL returned HTTP 404 at the time of fetching. No journal reference listed. The Dasgupta homepage lists it as a preprint. Wikipedia's Brumer–Stark article states that a full proof over Z 'has been announced' (2023). The paper's first part (read via the arXiv HTML) states Theorem 1.2 for a fixed prime p, 'proven for p odd in [dk]', so it suffices to prove p=2; the p=2 step uses Ribet's lemma 'proved in [ri]' (Section 2.7).
events.revisions: v1 25 Oct 2023 only, as far as the arXiv page shows; v2 URL returned 404 when fetched.
events.delivers: Per abstract: the Brumer–Stark conjecture over Z, i.e. for all primes including 2, in the setting of the paper's Theorem 1.2 (Fitting-ideal form, Fitt of the minus-part Pontryagin dual equals the Stickelberger-type ideal Theta/2^t) under hypotheses (A1)–(A5) for a fixed prime p. I read the first part of the text only; (A1)–(A5) and the last 56k characters were not read, so whether the hypotheses cover every abelian case of the Brumer–Stark statement is unverified. Scope in the Annals sense: H/F abelian CM with F totally real.
events.remains: Stark conjectures in general (non-abelian, higher-order, Artin L-functions at s=0 beyond the Brumer–Stark setting); the scope of Brumer–Stark outside the hypotheses (A1)–(A5), unverified; the 'strong' Brumer–Stark form used in the 2023 ETNC paper if it is a distinct statement, unverified.
events.time_since_posted: about 35 months (25 Oct 2023 to 13 Oct 2026); no journal acceptance found
events.doubts: (a) The p=2 step depends on Ribet's lemma in the residually indistinguishable case, proved in a separate preprint [ri] ('The Residually Indistinguishable Case of Ribet's Method for GL2', by the same four authors; see the 'residually indistinguishable' entry). I could not read or locate [ri] on arXiv, and the step is cited as proved there. (b) The authors' own companion exposition (arXiv:2310.16631) states the p=2 result as 'In [4], we prove the Brumer–Stark conjecture at p=2 using a suitably generalized version of Theorem 1.3', so the p=2 argument's only support found is by the same authors. (c) A seminar abstract by Rafah Hajjar Munoz (search snippet only, not opened, dated after 2023) says most generalisations of Ribet's lemma assume residual distinguishability and that the indistinguishable case is harder. It does not say that the Dasgupta et al. argument fails. (d) No referee report, erratum, withdrawal, objection or published independent check was found. (e) Dasgupta's homepage lists the paper as a preprint; the journal acceptance status is not established.
events.direction: Claims the Brumer–Stark conjecture holds at all primes, i.e. in the direction the conjecture asserts (Stickelberger annihilation over Z), with the p=2 case being the new content.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, Kakde, Silliman and Wang, 'The Residually Indistinguishable Case of Ribet's Method for GL2' (the [ri] of arXiv:2310.16399; no arXiv id found). Theorem: a general version of Ribet's lemma for GL2 without the residual-distinguishedness assumption. Cited as the source of the Ribet lemma used at p=2. The PDF (sites.math.duke.edu/~dasgupta/papers/RI.pdf) could not be read by WebFetch. Date known only as a year: a talk abstract is dated 15 Mar 2023 (Philadelphia NT seminar), and the 2023 DKSW paper cites it as proved.
events.delivers: Ribet's lemma for GL2 in the residually indistinguishable case (Theorem 1.3 of the exposition; Theorem 2.15 of DKSW). A tool used for p=2 in the Brumer–Stark argument. Not a Stark result by itself.
events.remains: This is a technical lemma; what it leaves open is not stated in the sources read.
events.doubts: This is the key input for the p=2 step of the DKSW proof. Its own posting date and status were not verified; its text could not be read.
events.direction: Tool supporting the claim at p=2.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, 'On Constructing Extensions of Residually Isomorphic Characters' (arXiv:2310.16631; v1 25 Oct 2023, single author). Exposition of the joint work with Kakde, Silliman and Wang that proves a version of Ribet's lemma for GL2 in the residually indistinguishable case. The exposition states: 'In [4], we prove the Brumer–Stark conjecture at p=2 using a suitably generalized version of Theorem 1.3.' Published as Springer Proc. Math. Stat. vol. 527 (2026), pp. 75–99 per Dasgupta's Duke listing (search result; not opened).
events.revisions: Springer Proceedings in Mathematics and Statistics vol. 527 (Jan 2026) per Duke listing.
events.delivers: A version of Ribet's lemma for GL2 in the residually indistinguishable case, with a statement that it is used to prove the Brumer–Stark conjecture at p=2 (per the exposition's own sentence). Tool, not a Stark result.
events.remains: Not applicable: a tool paper; the statement about Brumer–Stark at p=2 depends on the DKSW paper.

checked_by.who: Springer Proceedings in Mathematics and Statistics
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as vol. 527 (2026) per Duke listing (not opened)

events.doubts: Written by one of the four DKSW authors; not an independent check of the p=2 argument.
events.direction: Supports the p=2 claim in DKSW from the same team.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta, Kakde and Silliman, 'On The Equivariant Tamagawa Number Conjecture' (arXiv:2312.09849; v1 15 Dec 2023). Using the strong form of Brumer–Stark from the authors' previous work, deduces the minus part of the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for the Tate motive of K/F, integrally over Z. Cites Bullach, Burns, Daoud and Seo.
events.delivers: Conditional deduction: strong Brumer–Stark implies the minus part of the ETNC for the Tate motive of K/F, over Z. A consequence of Brumer–Stark, not a proof of it.
events.remains: Brumer–Stark itself is not established by this paper; ETNC beyond the minus part.
events.direction: Consequence of the Brumer–Stark result; does not decide Brumer–Stark.

events.what_happened: Arnau Padrés Masdemont, bachelor's thesis 'Stark's conjecture for representations attached to modular forms' (UPC, with UCL; advisor Luís García Martínez; tutor Víctor Rotger), 2024. It numerically checks Stark's conjecture (Tate's form) for several two-dimensional Artin representations of dihedral, tetrahedral and octahedral type, built from newforms via Deligne–Serre, including cases described as previously unpublished. Known from a search summary; the PDF was not readable by WebFetch, so the month and content are unverified.
events.delivers: Numerical verification of Stark units for finitely many two-dimensional Artin representations (per summary). Finite instances; not a proof of the conjecture for any class.
events.remains: The Stark conjecture for all Artin representations; the non-numerical cases.

checked_by.who: Luís García Martínez (advisor); Víctor Rotger (tutor), UPC
checked_by.qualification: Faculty in number theory at UPC
checked_by.what_they_did: Supervised the bachelor's thesis; approval not verified

events.doubts: Numerical checks on finitely many representations, not a proof; the thesis could not be read, so its exact claims are from a summary.
events.direction: Consistent with Stark in the checked cases; finitely many instances, which move no quantity in the conjecture's general statement.

events.what_happened: Kairi Black, 'A refinement of the Stark conjectures over ATR fields' (Duke University PhD dissertation, 2025; hdl.handle.net/10161/34094). Per search summaries of the abstract and research statement: for number fields with exactly one complex embedding, proposes a refinement of Stark's conjectures that describes the units themselves rather than their absolute values. Main theorem: a derivative of a partial zeta function is expressed through Shintani-type sums of log-gamma/Barnes functions modulo 2πi Z. The unit formula is stated as a conjecture. DukeSpace was blocked by a bot check; the dissertation was not read.
events.delivers: Per summary: the main theorem relating a partial zeta derivative to Shintani-type sums, modulo 2πi Z, for ATR fields. A restricted class (one complex place).
events.remains: The unit formula (Stark units as exponentials of the sums) is a conjecture in the dissertation; the general Stark conjecture.
events.direction: Partial result in a restricted class; the unit formula is conjectural in the source.

events.what_happened: Mahesh Kakde awarded the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries (ICTP and IMU). Secondary reports say the citation recognises his work on noncommutative Iwasawa theory and his 'outstanding work on the Gross-Stark and Brumer-Stark conjectures'. Dates differ across reports: 30 Sep 2026 (ICTP/IMU, per one report), 7 Oct 2026 (IISc), 9 Oct 2026 (Drishti IAS). The ICTP/IMU page was not opened.
events.revisions: Report dates differ (30 Sep, 7 Oct, 9 Oct 2026); the 30 Sep date is from a single secondary report.
events.delivers: Nothing new mathematically: a recognition of prior work, including Brumer–Stark and Gross–Stark work.
events.remains: All of the problem, as the prize announces no new result.
events.direction: Not applicable: an award, not a result.

events.what_happened: Abreu and Speckbacher, 'Optimal concentration in the Paley-Wiener space' (arXiv:2607.19192; v1 21 Jul 2026). The abstract proves that intervals optimise concentration of L2 mass for functions in the Paley–Wiener space of band-limited functions. The abstract does not mention Donoho or Stark. A survey (arXiv:2608.24961, 'The Gold Rush in AI4Math', Table 3 row 49) lists this paper under 'Donoho Stark conjecture', 1989, outcome 'proved', credited to 'OpenAI GPT 5.6 Sol; OpenAI GPT-5.5 Pro', and says the outcome was inferred by an LLM-based review of the authors' descriptions, not independently verified.

summary: Sources, in order of weight: the Annals paper (Dasgupta–Kakde, 2023, arXiv 2020) proves the Brumer–Stark conjecture for every prime except 2; the arXiv preprint of Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang (arXiv:2310.16399, 25 Oct 2023) claims a complete proof over Z, including 2. I read the first part of the DKSW text via arXiv HTML and ar5iv; it proves Theorem 1.2 for a fixed p and reduces the problem to p=2, which it handles with a Ribet-lemma result proved in a companion paper [ri] that I could not locate or read. The DKSW abstract page shows only v1, and the v2 URL returned 404. I found no journal acceptance, referee report, erratum or independent public check; Dasgupta's own homepage lists the paper as a preprint. The 2023 Wikipedia Brumer–Stark article says a full proof over Z has been announced, while its paraphrased lead still says few cases are known; I read those articles through a summariser, not verbatim. Close call one: whether DKSW counts as settling the Brumer–Stark conjecture depends on (A1)–(A5) in its Theorem 1.2, which I did not read, and on the companion lemma. Close call two: the problem also names the general Stark conjectures, and for these I found no proof in the window. Partial results include Zhang's Stark–Harris–Venkatesh compatibility (v4 Jun 2024), Nickel's totally-odd-character strong Stark (PAMS 2024), Bullach–Macías Castillo on Rubin and BKS cases (2023, journal 2025), Burns–Macías–Seo refined Stark (2023), Padrés numerical checks (2024 thesis), and Black's refinement for ATR fields (2025 dissertation, unit formula conjectural). The Brumer–Stark unit formula is handled by Honnor (v1 Feb 2023; v3 Dec 2025, reported to resolve the 2-ambiguity) and by Dasgupta–Honnor–Spieß (arXiv Nov 2022; JLMS Oct 2025, which says 'essentially proven'). The Brumer–Stark unit-formula result (Honnor v3) and the 2-part of the unit formula are not settled by any source I could read. AI search: I searched for AI involvement in Stark and Brumer–Stark repeatedly, including AlphaEvolve, GPT, Gemini, Claude, AlphaProof, Aristotle, Lean and mathlib, Erdős-problem trackers and an AI4Math survey. No source I found names an AI system in any Stark or Brumer–Stark result. The only AI credit touching 'Stark' is the survey credit for Donoho–Stark (a different problem), which rests on an LLM review, not the authors. The Kakde 2026 prize is an award, not a result. No Lean or Coq formalisation was found; one search for mathlib found nothing. I also checked for later papers citing DKSW: DKS (Dec 2023) builds on a 'previous result giving a strong form' of Brumer–Stark, and Honnor's v2 (Jan 2024; not opened) describes the work as showing the conjecture holds. Neither is an independent check.
competing_reading: Read DKSW as a proved theorem: the claim is by experienced authors, the away-from-2 part is refereed in the Annals, the p=2 step is a targeted extension of a lemma already proven by the same team, and the 2025–2026 literature (Honnor v3, DHS JLMS) builds on the result without objection. On that reading the Brumer–Stark conjecture was settled in October 2023 and only the general Stark conjecture remains. The opposite reading: a preprint without journal acceptance after about 35 months, with a single version, a key lemma in an unread companion paper, no independent public engagement and an unverified (A1)–(A5) hypothesis set, is a claim, not a settled result; the honest status is 'announced, unrefereed as far as found'. Each reading gives a different count for the Brumer–Stark part of the problem, and the choice is for the judging pass.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Journal acceptance of arXiv:2310.16399 (or a referee report) and a second arXiv version. (2) The companion Ribet-lemma paper [ri] on arXiv or its acceptance, and an independent expert check of its use at p=2. (3) The text of (A1)–(A5) in DKSW Theorem 1.2 and the last 56k characters of the paper, to confirm the hypothesis scope and the proof of p=2. (4) A published expert digest of the over-Z proof. For the general Stark conjecture: a proof in the non-abelian or higher-order setting, none found in the window.

judgement.why: The statement names the Stark conjectures in general and Brumer–Stark, so even a complete Brumer–Stark proof is a case, not the whole. DKSW (25 Oct 2023) is the strongest Brumer–Stark event, but it predates the snapshot and has had no outside check (case, unreviewed). Dasgupta–Kakde away from 2 and Stark 1980 are journal-digested pre-snapshot cases. Function-field, p-adic, Gross–Stark, unit-formula and refinement results change the question, so they are variants. Surveys, tool lemmas and conditional consequences are none. Of the post-snapshot events, Padrés is finite numerics with a year-only 2024 date (instances, null date). Black's main theorem is a zeta-derivative identity whose unit formula is still conjectural (none). The prize is an award (none). Donoho–Stark is a different problem (variant), and its AI credit rests on an LLM survey, not the authors. Journal re-publications in the window (Nickel PAMS 2024, DHS 2025, Bullach–Macías Castillo 2025, Honnor v3) do not re-date earlier first arguments, except that Honnor v3 may contain new mathematics. Even so, that is a variant.
judgement.doubts: Honnor v3 (Dec 2025) reportedly removes the 2-ambiguity in the Brumer–Stark unit formula, which is new mathematics inside the window. I treated it as a refinement (variant) rather than a case of the statement. Black's dissertation was not read, so its main theorem could be judged a case of a Stark refinement over ATR fields; I scored it none.
